title: Listening to classical records in the Norvo band
summary: The band bought classical sets; jazz people loved Stravinsky and symphonic music, contrary to Hammond.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Yes. My brother began buying them at

at this time and I began listening and of course so did Red and Mildred and so did the guys in the band. If they weren't going to clubs listening, we bought a record player. of our own and we listened to these things. It was sessions like that that I first came on (inaudible), and Le sacre du printemps.

If you think that the jazz people didn't go for this, you're crazy; they did. John Hammond was always saying how Mildred wanted small bands; not true; Mildred loved big bands and loved symphonic music and would have it on in her home, and I was part of that too. We'd all get knocked out by the various things that were happening.
This goes back even ten years before that with (inaudible) and all those people; right?
I guess so. Maybe that's where Mildred got it. Who knows? She was contemporary with him. It could be.
I don't know, but I would be one bit surprised. Whiteman with Gershwin.
Most people who get involved seriously with their horn are not turned off by this, and even more sparked by it; I know that Charlie Parker was. I know that because he told me so.
Most of the harmonic things that have come into jazz in the last forty years have come from twentieth century classical music.
Or it could go the other way. I think it's part of the air.
